title: Grade 5 ELA — Reading and Comparing Short Texts
subject: English Language Arts
description: Practice with questions on summary, evidence, paraphrase, inference.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Text A: Our town painted bike lanes on Main Street to make space for riders. Text B: Riders asked for a rack next to the market so they could lock their bikes. What do both texts describe?
choices: reasons to close the market
how to fix a flat tire
plans to widen highways
ways a town can support people who bike

questions.question: Text A: Our town painted bike lanes on Main Street to make space for riders. Text B: Riders asked for a rack next to the market so they could lock their bikes. Which detail comes only from Text B?
choices: The town uses streets.
The changes concern biking.
The town painted Main Street bike lanes.
Riders asked for a place to lock bikes.

questions.question: Text A: Volunteers carried records upstairs before the river flooded the library. Text B: After flooding, neighbors helped dry books and replace wet shelves. How do the texts differ?
choices: A describes cleanup; B describes preparing.
A is about a school flood; B is about forest fires.
A describes preparing for a flood; B describes cleanup.
A describes repairs; B explains why it rained.

questions.question: Text A: Volunteers carried records upstairs before the river flooded the library. Text B: After flooding, neighbors helped dry books and replace wet shelves. Which summary covers both?
choices: A river flooded because books were moved.
People helped protect and restore a library around the time of a flood.
Neighbors rebuilt an entire town before a storm.
Volunteers closed a library and never returned.

questions.question: Text A: Wood chips spread over garden soil slowed water loss. Text B: Fallen leaves covered the soil and decomposed into organic matter. What do both materials do at first?
choices: stop all rain from falling
pull seeds out of the ground
turn soil to plastic
cover the soil

questions.question: Text A: Wood chips spread over garden soil slowed water loss. Text B: Fallen leaves covered the soil and decomposed into organic matter. What result is stated only in Text B?
choices: Water loss slowed.
The material decomposed into organic matter.
The garden got more rain.
The soil was covered.

questions.question: Text A: An owl hunts after dark and can find prey with its hearing. Text B: A hawk often hunts during the day and can see small prey from far away. Which contrast is supported?
choices: Both birds only hunt after dark.
The owl cannot hunt moving prey.
The hawk hunts only by hearing.
The texts emphasize hearing for the owl and sight for the hawk.

questions.question: Text A: An owl hunts after dark and can find prey with its hearing. Text B: A hawk often hunts during the day and can see small prey from far away. Which detail supports a claim about the owl's hearing?
choices: It has large wings.
It can find prey using sound after dark.
It can see small prey from far away.
It always hunts beside water.

questions.question: Text A: The school counted 80 plastic bottles in the trash one week. Text B: After a refill station opened, the school counted 45 bottles the next week. What does the comparison show?
choices: The second week's count was lower.
Bottles became heavier.
The first count was smaller.
The refill station opened years earlier.

questions.question: Text A: The school counted 80 plastic bottles in the trash one week. Text B: After a refill station opened, the school counted 45 bottles the next week. Which claim needs more evidence?
choices: One count was 80.
The station was open by the second count.
The station caused all of the drop in bottles.
The second count was 45.

questions.question: Text A: A diary describes a winter market and the smell of fresh bread. Text B: A store ledger lists loaves sold and prices for each day. Which source gives the writer's personal experience directly?
choices: Text A
neither text
Text B
both texts equally

questions.question: Text A: A diary describes a winter market and the smell of fresh bread. Text B: A store ledger lists loaves sold and prices for each day. Which question is Text B best suited to answer?
choices: How many loaves were sold each day?
How did buyers feel about the bread?
What did the baker feel about winter?
What did each loaf smell like?

questions.question: Text A: A class built birdhouses with small doors for small birds. Text B: A class built bat boxes with narrow gaps for bats to enter. Which shared idea fits both?
choices: A shelter's entrance can suit the animal that uses it.
Neither shelter needs an entrance.
Bats and birds use identical shelters.
All animals need the same door size.

questions.question: Text A: A class built birdhouses with small doors for small birds. Text B: A class built bat boxes with narrow gaps for bats to enter. Which difference is stated in the texts?
choices: Only the bat shelter was built by students.
Both groups studied bats.
One shelter uses a small door; the other uses a narrow gap.
The birdhouse was put in a cave.

questions.question: Text A: The long trail stays on firm ground most of the year. Text B: The short route passes low ground that turns muddy after storms. Which route would a hiker likely choose to avoid mud after rain?
choices: the short route
neither route because both are stated to flood
the long trail
either one because the ground is described as the same

questions.question: Text A: The long trail stays on firm ground most of the year. Text B: The short route passes low ground that turns muddy after storms. What is one tradeoff shown in the texts?
choices: The shorter route may be muddier.
The short path is farther from its start.
Both paths are always dry.
The longer route closes every day.

questions.question: Text A: A gardener trimmed some tomato leaves to let more light reach the fruit. Text B: Another gardener put straw under the plants to cover bare soil. What goal is shared?
choices: Both removed straw from the soil.
Both gardeners changed how they cared for tomato plants.
Both sold the same harvest.
Both tried to reduce light on the fruit.

questions.question: Text A: A gardener trimmed some tomato leaves to let more light reach the fruit. Text B: Another gardener put straw under the plants to cover bare soil. What problem is the second action most directly meant to address?
choices: tangled leaves around each fruit
too little light on the fruit
exposed soil
a missing garden fence

questions.question: Text A: The class placed signs near a stream asking hikers to stay on the path. Text B: The parks crew later counted fewer footprints on the streambank. What do the texts together suggest?
choices: Footprints made the class move the stream.
The crew moved the trail before signs went up.
The signs caused every footprint to vanish.
The signs may have encouraged hikers to use the path.

questions.question: Text A: The class placed signs near a stream asking hikers to stay on the path. Text B: The parks crew later counted fewer footprints on the streambank. Which follow-up would strengthen the inference?
choices: Measure the height of a nearby school.
Compare footprint counts across several similar weeks before and after the signs.
Count the number of letters in one sign.
Ask how many kinds of fish live elsewhere.
